A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ChroKnowledge work. Their main text, figures, tables, mathematical definitions and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching relocated related work, prompting results and templates.

before.justification: v1 reports original temporal-knowledge evaluations across five domains and chronological-prompting experiments in Sections 5–7 and the appendices, including Tables 3–4.

after.justification: v2 retains original experiments and adds True/False evaluations, additional models, and analyses separating changed from unchanged objects, including Tables 5–7.

M1.justification: Section 2.2 extends ChroKnowledge's elicitation interface from generation and MCQA to include True/False assertions and responses. This is a limited procedural extension. ChroKnowPrompt's temporal traversal, majority voting and iterative refinement remain unchanged, as do both appendix algorithms.

E1.justification: v2 adds binary fact verification through True/False evaluations across the existing domains. The five domains, underlying sources, time ranges and dataset sizes remain unchanged. Separating changed and unchanged objects analyzes existing coverage rather than introducing another dataset.

E2.justification: Gemini-1.5-flash joins the benchmark and prompting comparisons. Tables 6–7 additionally evaluate mpt-7b-chat, Pythia-Chat-Base-7B and nemotron-3-8b-chat-4k-sft-hf. The original model comparisons remain; newly discussed temporal knowledge graph methods are not experimentally evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: The added experiments introduce Boolean-answer testing with timestamped assertions and demonstrations, additional chat-model configurations, and separate reporting for changed versus unchanged objects. Existing experiments retain the 10% prompting subset, fuzzy-matching threshold of 70, sampling temperatures and greedy prompting evaluation.

E4.justification: v2 adds a central diagnostic analysis separating prompting gains on changed and unchanged objects (Table 5), tests effectiveness on additional chat models, and compares object-change distributions in the benchmark and correctly recalled knowledge (Figures 2–4 and 8). The previous-versus-total-span analysis already existed in v1.

E5.justification: Both versions retain five exemplar samplings for categorization and fixed-seed inference, without adding repeated-run uncertainty estimates, confidence intervals or significance tests. Figure 8's new means, standard deviations and skewness describe dataset heterogeneity rather than uncertainty in experimental performance.

E6.justification: v2 adds True/False scores, additional-model results, object-change statistics and subgroup findings. For example, Table 5 splits GPT-4o-mini's previously reported general-dynamic gain of 7.7 into 0.7 for changed and 7.0 for unchanged objects. Original model rows from v1 Tables 3–4 remain unchanged in v2 Tables 6–7; revised aggregate figures do not establish same-setting performance changes.

T1.justification: The set-based knowledge definitions in Table 1, chronological categories and algorithmic specifications are retained. The new object-level rationale and temporal knowledge graph comparison are conceptual discussions, without new formal assumptions, theorems, proofs or derivations.

C1.justification: v1 emphasizes evaluating and updating knowledge across the entire timeline. v2 recasts ChroKnowledge primarily as evaluation and explicitly restricts its strongest prompting claims to recalling unchanged objects. The abstract, introduction and conclusion foreground difficulties with dynamic knowledge and unstructured formats, materially narrowing the advertised contribution.

C2.justification: Beyond v1's broad general/legal-domain limitations, v2 explains that prompting gains concentrate on unchanged objects and that recovering historical object changes remains difficult. It adds interpretations concerning template dependence and bias toward low-change objects. The temporal knowledge graph comparison also acknowledges that the benchmark may overlook broader event interdependencies.

D1.justification: Appendix A.8 and Table 4 newly disclose the exact generation and verification/refinement system prompts, while Table 9 documents the True/False template. These improve implementation documentation without establishing a changed prompting algorithm. Existing preprocessing, inference hardware, precision and code/data access information are retained.

R1.justification: Appendices A.3.2–A.3.3 and Table 3 substantially expand positioning against temporal knowledge graphs, arguing for object-level tracking of gradual changes and discussing comparative limitations. New citations support this discussion and the added evaluations. The existing parametric/non-parametric editing review moves from Section 8.2 to Appendix A.1 rather than being removed.

P1.justification: The abstract, results discussion and conclusion undergo substantial rewriting. Section 7.2 becomes a broader analysis section, legal-domain findings move into the main narrative, and editing-related work and task configurations move into the appendix. The appendix is reorganized around expanded benchmark explanations and experimental analyses.

P2.justification: The principal domain plots are redesigned from line charts into heatmap, radar-chart and distribution panels. Benchmark and prompting diagrams are revised, prompting transitions receive a new main-text figure, and existing span tables move to the appendix with expanded rows. New comparison tables, distributions and full-timeline radar plots substantially change the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: The changed/unchanged analysis makes the limits of prompting clearer and supports better-qualified claims; broader evaluations and explicit system prompts also strengthen the paper. Reporting inconsistencies temper these benefits: Section 7.2 repeats biomedical span averages of 11.9/6.1 despite Table 6 reporting 12.1/6.8, and Figure 7 reports a GPT-4o-mini general-dynamic unchanged-object gain of 6.3 versus Table 5's 7.0 without reconciliation.
